students.who: A class 9 student who is okay at maths but rushes.
students.belief: √2 is halfway between 1 and 2, so it must be 1.5.
students.temperament: Tries the board first, presses Check quickly, asks Jugnu after a wrong Check. Short messages.
students.understanding: √2 is the number whose square is 2; 1.5² = 2.25 is too big, so √2 is less than 1.5, about 1.41–1.42.

students.who: A class 9 student from a Hindi-medium school who finds decimals scary.
students.belief: Squaring a decimal works like squaring the digits: 1.4 × 1.4 = 1.16.
students.temperament: Gets discouraged after two wrong tries and asks Jugnu to just tell the answer. Writes very short messages.
students.writes: Hindi in Devanagari, with English maths words
students.understanding: 1.4 × 1.4 = 1.96; reading the square under the line shows how close to 2 each guess is; √2 is between 1.41 and 1.42.

students.who: A class 9 student who thinks of numbers as whole steps.
students.belief: There is no number between 1.4 and 1.5, because 1.5 comes right after 1.4.
students.temperament: Polite, asks Jugnu early, follows suggestions literally.
students.writes: Hinglish in Latin letters ("bhai 1.4 ke baad toh 1.5 hi aata hai na")
students.understanding: Adding another decimal place gives numbers like 1.41, 1.45 between them; there are always more.

students.who: A class 10 student who has seen house wiring at home.
students.belief: Every bulb gets the full 1.5 V from the cell, and taking one bulb out leaves the other glowing, like lights at home.
students.temperament: Confident; picks an answer early and argues a bit when told it's wrong. Experiments on the board if asked to.
students.understanding: In series there is one path: the bulbs share the 1.5 V (0.75 V each) and taking one out breaks the path, so B goes out.

students.who: A class 10 student who learnt that a cell gives a fixed current.
students.belief: The cell always gives the same current, so the main ammeter stays at 0.45 A whatever you do with the switch.
students.temperament: Curious, asks why a lot, but reluctant to touch the circuit in case it breaks.
students.understanding: Each branch takes its own current (V ÷ R): A takes 0.3 A, B 0.15 A; the main current is their sum, so opening S leaves 0.3 A.

students.who: A class 10 student who doesn't read circuit diagrams yet.
students.belief: Any switch turns on any bulb; you just keep tapping until it works.
students.temperament: Taps things randomly, rarely reads; asks 'what do i do' when stuck.
students.understanding: Each switch is in one bulb's branch; close S₂ (B's branch) and open S₁ (A's branch).

students.who: A class 9 student who likes patterns.
students.belief: 1 ÷ 7 must repeat 7 digits, because you divide by 7.
students.temperament: Answers before tapping much; impatient; says 'just tell me' after one wrong try.
students.understanding: The remainders can only be 1 to 6, so a remainder repeats within 6 steps; 1 ÷ 7 = 0.142857… repeats 6 digits.

students.who: A class 8 student who thinks probability means exact shares.
students.belief: A fair coin gives exactly half heads after 100 tosses, every time.
students.temperament: Likes pressing buttons; will toss if it's suggested, then argues with what they see at first.
students.understanding: Each toss is random; the fraction of heads gets close to ½ with many tosses but isn't exactly ½ every time.
